entries.desc: Truth source clearly separates Koala CLI, Runner CLI/Mac runner, and Python Authority responsibilities.

evidence.command: rg -n "Koala CLI — workflow client|Koala Runner CLI / Mac Runner — execution plane|Python Authority — receipt authority" docs/requirements/decisions/authority-client-role.md
evidence.note: Lines 53/57/61 define CLI as workflow client, Runner/Mac as execution plane, and Python Authority as receipt authority.

entries.desc: Docs explain that putting CLI and runner in one repo/package does not by itself make evidence authoritative.

evidence.command: rg -n "No overclaim by colocation|does not make CLI-shaped evidence authoritative" docs/requirements/decisions/authority-client-role.md
evidence.note: Doc includes the explicit no-overclaim-by-colocation boundary.

entries.desc: Docs forbid claiming CLI local/shadow evidence or accepted-only POST responses as L2+ production authority receipts.

evidence.command: rg -n "Transport acceptance is NOT receipt verification|not L2\+ authority|receipt-backed-l2-plus" docs/requirements/decisions/authority-client-role.md
evidence.note: Doc forbids treating accepted-only transport or CLI local/shadow evidence as L2+ receipt-backed authority.

entries.desc: Authority envelope or submission decision exposes a local/shadow/thin-client classification that downstream code/tests can assert.

evidence.note: Classifier and authority-submit wrapper expose local-only/thin-client/receipt-backed classes with L2+ requirements including independent verifier run and command/transcript/diff hashes.

entries.desc: Enforce transport success based only on accepted=true is not described or typed as verified server receipt authority.

evidence.note: Existing authority client smoke remains compatible; authority-submit comment and wrapper label accepted=true as transport acceptance, not receipt verification.

entries.desc: A smoke test proves missing producerRunId/verifierRunId/provider/model/vendor/hash/receipt fields cannot be upgraded to a production L2+ claim.

evidence.note: Smoke proves missing run/provider/model/vendor/hash/signature/receipt fields, same-run verifier collapse, and accepted=true cannot upgrade CLI evidence to receipt-backed L2+. Output: ✓ authority boundary smoke passed: CLI evidence is local/shadow/thin-client, not receipt-backed L2+ authority.

entries.desc: Local/off mode remains usable and clearly classified as local evidence.

evidence.note: Smoke covers off mode as local-only and prints the user-visible non-receipt-backed thin-client boundary line.

entries.desc: Shadow/enforce transport failures keep existing behavior but warning/error text does not overclaim receipt-backed authority.

evidence.note: Existing shadow/enforce authority evidence flow smoke still passes, preserving transport behavior while new wording prevents receipt-backed overclaim.

entries.desc: A forged/local-only authority success path cannot pass a smoke assertion that requires server receipt-backed authority.

evidence.note: Adversarial cases prove forged partial fields, missing hashes, same-run verifier collapse, and accepted=true do not pass receipt-backed L2+ classification.

entries.desc: Focused authority/client smoke tests pass and prove the boundary classification.

evidence.command: npm run build && npm run test:authority-boundary-smoke && npm run test:authority-client && npm run test:authority-evidence-flow
evidence.note: Build plus focused boundary/client/evidence-flow smokes pass and prove the boundary classification.

entries.desc: The story output explicitly says Runner CLI/Mac and Python authority work are separate follow-up stories.

evidence.note: Docs state B-ec09 completes only M1; M2 is Python authority policy discovery, M5/FU-4 is Mac/Runner work, M3-M6 remain routed in the table, and no follow-up is auto-opened.
